Rashi on Berakhot 18a:10:1.english: A saddlebag [disakaya] - A large leather bag.

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:10:2.english: And if he was afraid - And he needs to ride on the horse and run [fast].

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:11:1.hebrew: אלא אסיפא - אם היה מתירא, רוכב:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:11:1.english: Rather, to the latter clause - If he was afraid, he [may] ride [upon it].

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:12:1.hebrew: מלוה ה' חונן דל - קרי ביה: מלוה את המקום מי שחונן את הדל. ואין לך דל מן המת, והמלוה אותו, כאלו מלוה את המקום:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:12:1.english: He who lends to the Lord is gracious to the poor - Read in it: One who is gracious to the poor lends to the Omnipresent. And you have no poor person [greater] than the deceased; and one who escorts him, [it is] as if he lends to the Omnipresent.

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:14:1.hebrew: לא שנית - לא חזרת עליו פעם שנית, כדי שתתבונן בו:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:14:1.english: You did not repeat [it] - You did not review it a second time in order to reflect upon it.

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:14:2.hebrew: אלו צדיקים - ומאי יודעים שימותו? נותנים אל לבם יום המיתה, ומושכים ידיהם מן העבירה. ורשעים אינם יודעים מאומה — שעושים עצמם כאינם יודעים, וחוטאים:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:14:2.english: These are the righteous - And what is [the meaning of] "they know that they will die"? They take the day of death to heart and withdraw their hands from sin. And [as for] the wicked, "they know nothing" — for they make themselves as if they do not know, and sin.

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:14:3.hebrew: הוא הכה - השפיל את השנים של דורות משני מקדשים, שלא היה בהם כמותו:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:14:3.english: He smote - He humbled the two [sets of] generations from the two Temples, for there was no one like him among them.

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:14:4.hebrew: אריאל - זה בית המקדש, שנא': הוי אריאל אריאל קרית חנה דוד (ישעיהו כ״ט:א׳):
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:14:4.english: Ariel - This is the Holy Temple, as it is stated: "Ah, Ariel, Ariel, the city where David encamped" (Isaiah 29:1).

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:14:5.hebrew: מואב - על שם שבנאו דוד, דאתי מרות המואביה:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:14:5.english: Moab - [So called] because David, who descended from Ruth the Moabitess, built it.

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:1:1.hebrew: ואין מברכין עליו - אין צריך שיברכו לו אחרים בברכת הלחם:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:1:1.english: And they do not recite a blessing for him - There is no need for others to recite a blessing for him with the blessing over bread.

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:1:2.hebrew: ואין מזמנין עליו - אין מצטרף עם שלשה לזימון:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:1:2.english: And they do not recite a zimmun for him - He does not combine with [them to form] three for a zimmun.

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:2:1.hebrew: תשמיש המטה איכא בינייהו - לר"ש, חייב אבל בעונה בשבת:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:2:1.english: Conjugal relations is [the difference] between them - According to Rabban Shimon [ben Gamliel], a mourner is obligated in [the mitzvah of] conjugal relations on Shabbat.

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:3:1.hebrew: קתני מיהת פטור מק"ש ומכל ברכות - ואפילו כשהוא אוכל בבית חבירו:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:3:1.english: In any event, it teaches [that he is] exempt from the recitation of Shema and from all blessings - And [this applies] even when he eats in his friend's house.

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:3:2.hebrew: תרגמא - להא דתני פטור, אמי שאין לו בית אחר, דקאמר מחזיר פניו ואוכל:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:3:2.english: Explain it - [Explain] that which [the baraita] teaches, "[he is] exempt," [as referring] to one who has no other room, where it says: "he turns his face away and eats."

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:3:3.hebrew: רב אשי אמר - לעולם אכולא. ומתניתין נמי, אפילו בבית אחר נמי פטר ליה, דכל שמוטל עליו לקוברו קרי מוטל לפניו:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:3:3.english: Rav Ashi said - Actually, [the exemption applies] to the entire [baraita]; and our mishna also exempts him even in another house, for as long as it is incumbent upon him to bury him, [the deceased] is called "laid out before him."

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:3:4.hebrew: ויקם אברהם וגו' וכתיב ואקברה מתי מלפני - וההיא שעתא לאו לפניו הוה:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:3:4.english: “And Abraham rose up,” etc., and it is written: “that I may bury my dead from before me” - And at that time, [the deceased] was not before him.

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:4:1.hebrew: משמרו - אדם אחר שאינו קרובו, אלא משמרו:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:4:1.english: [One who] watches over him - Another person, who is not his relative, but rather [merely] watches over him.

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:7:1.hebrew: תופס ד' אמות לק"ש - שאסור לקרות בתוך ארבע אמות שלו, משום לועג לרש:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:7:1.english: [The deceased] occupies four cubits with regard to the recitation of Shema - That it is forbidden to recite [the Shema] within four cubits of him, on account of [the prohibition of] "one who mocks the poor."

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:8:1.english: [He is] exempt from the recitation of Shema - Because he is engaged in a mitzvah.

Rashi on Berakhot 18a:9:1.hebrew: חוששין לעכברים - תנא קמא חייש לעכברים, אפילו בספינה:
Rashi on Berakhot 18a:9:1.english: [Whether] we are concerned about mice - The first Tanna is concerned about mice, even on a boat.

Tosafot on Berakhot 18a:10:1.hebrew: וירכב עליהם - אבל אי מפשילן לאחוריו על החמור, שפיר דמי. וכן בס"ת; ואפילו אם בדעתך לאסור ס"ת — אבל בנביאים ובכתובים שפיר דמי, מדנקט ס"ת. ולא מסתבר לומר משום שריותא דנכרים ולסטים, דהא פשיטא דמותר, דלמה יהיה אסור? ועוד, דבהדיא אמר בירושלמי: דסקיא מלאה ספרים או שהיו בה עצמות של מת, הרי זה מפשילן לאחוריו ורוכב עליו:
Tosafot on Berakhot 18a:10:1.english: "And ride on them" - However, if he slings them behind him on the donkey, it is permitted. And so too with a Torah scroll; and even if you are inclined to prohibit [doing so with] a Torah scroll, nevertheless with [scrolls of] the Prophets and the Writings it is permitted, since [the baraita] specified "a Torah scroll." And it is not reasonable to say [that this is permitted only] because of the dispensation for [fear of] gentiles and highwaymen, for it is obvious that it is permitted — for why would it be forbidden? And furthermore, it explicitly stated in the Yerushalmi: "A saddlebag full of scrolls, or in which there were bones of a deceased person — he slings them behind him and rides on it [the animal]."

Tosafot on Berakhot 18a:11:1.english: "Rather, to the latter clause" — [that] because of highwaymen it is permitted to ride on them - And the same law applies that [placing it] behind him is permitted, even without highwaymen.

Tosafot on Berakhot 18a:13:1.hebrew: למחר באין אצלנו ועכשיו מחרפין אותנו - ותימה: והא אמרי' בפ' התכלת (מנחות דף מא.): "ההיא שעתא ודאי רמינן ליה" — פי' נותנין ציצית בטליתותיהן — משום "לועג לרש"?! וי"ל, דה"פ: הכא דמביישין אותם במה שהחיים מצווים והמתים אינם מצווים, וגדול המצווה וכו'. וההיא דהתכלת — היינו דרמו חוטים למתים. ועכשיו אנו מסלקין אותן, ומאי שנא? אומר ר"ת: דוקא הם, שהיו רגילים כולם בחייהם ללבוש טלית בד' כנפות וללבוש ציצית, וגם לכל העוסקים בהם יש להם ציצית — והוה לועג לרש אם לא היה להם ציצית; או משום דכתיב "לדורתם" — לדור תם. אבל אנו, שגם בחיינו אין מנהגינו ללבוש תמיד ציצית — אי הוי רמינן להו, הוי כמו לועג לרש. וכ"ת: נשים לאותם שהיה להם בחייהם — א"כ יהיה לועג לרש לאחרים. ועוד אר"ת, ששמע מאנשי לותי"ר דמסירים הציצית, דציצית עולה למנין תרי"ג עם ח' חוטין וחמשה קשרים, ואם לובש ציצית נראה כאילו קיים כל התורה ומיחזי כשיקרא. וזה לא נהירא: דגם חיים עתה, למה לובשים? הלא לא קיימו כל התורה כולה! ומיהו י"ל, דאנו סומכים על מסכת שמחות (פי"ב), שצוה אבא שאול לבניו: "הטילו תכלת מאפיליוני". ואע"פ שהגמרא חולק עליו, יש דברים שאנו מניחין הגמ' שלנו ואנו עושין כספרים החיצונים — כמו מחזון ישעיהו כפסיקתא, וכמו ויחל, שיש בגמ' (מגילה דף לא.) דבתענית קורין ברכות וקללות, ובמס' סופרים (פי"ז) מפרש ויחל. והריצב"א היה רגיל שלא להסירם מן הכנף, אלא לקושרם ולהדקם בתוך הכנף לאפוקי נפשיה מפלוגתא: אם הם חייבין בציצית יש להם ציצית, ואם לאו הרי הם מכוסין:
Tosafot on Berakhot 18a:13:1.english: "Tomorrow they will come to us, and now they insult us" - And it is difficult: For didn't we say in the chapter [entitled] "HaTekhelet" (Menachot 41a): "At that time, we certainly cast [fringes] for him" — that is, they place tzitzit on their garments [i.e., shrouds] — because of "[Whoever] mocks the poor [blasphemes his Maker]"?! And one can say that this is the explanation: Here, [they are insulting them] because they shame them by the fact that the living are commanded [in mitzvot] while the dead are not commanded, and "greater is one who is commanded [and performs than one who is not commanded and performs], etc." And that [statement] in [the chapter of] HaTekhelet means that they cast threads for the dead [themselves]. And now [in our time], we remove them [from the shrouds] — and what is different? Rabbeinu Tam says: Specifically they [in Talmudic times affixed them], for during their lifetimes they were all accustomed to wear a four-cornered cloak and wear tzitzit, and all those attending to them [at burial] also had tzitzit; thus it would have been "mocking the poor" if they [the deceased] did not have tzitzit; or because it is written: "Throughout their generations [ledorotam]" (Numbers 15:38) — [which is expounded as] "for a whole [i.e., blameless] generation [ledor tam]." However, as for us, since even during our lifetimes it is not our practice to always wear tzitzit, if we were to cast [fringes] upon them, it would be like mocking the poor. And if you will say: Let us place [tzitzit] for those who had them during their lifetimes — if so, it would be "mocking the poor" toward the others [who did not wear them]. And furthermore, Rabbeinu Tam said that he heard from the people of Lotharingia that they remove the tzitzit because [the word] tzitzit equals the numerical value of 613 along with eight threads and five knots, and if he wears tzitzit, it appears as though he fulfilled the entire Torah, and it looks like a falsehood. But this is not plausible: For the living now as well — why do they wear [them]? Did they not also fail to fulfill the entire Torah?! However, one can say that we rely on Tractate Semachot (ch. 12), where Abba Shaul commanded his sons: "Remove [or: untie] the sky-blue [strings] from my cloak." And even though the Gemara disagrees with him, there are matters in which we set aside our Gemara and act in accordance with the external books — such as [reading the haftarot from] "Chazon Yeshayahu" according to the Pesikta, and like "Vayechal," for it states in the Gemara (Megillah 31a) that on a fast day we read the Blessings and Curses, whereas in Tractate Soferim (ch. 17) it explains [that we read] "Vayechal." And the Ritzba was accustomed not to remove them from the corner, but rather to tie them and tuck them tightly inside the corner, in order to remove himself from the dispute: If they [the dead] are obligated in tzitzit, they have tzitzit; and if not, behold, they are covered.

Tosafot on Berakhot 18a:14:1.english: "The two altar-hearths of Moab" - [So called] on account of David and Solomon, who built the Temple and descended from Ruth the Moabitess.

Tosafot on Berakhot 18a:6:1.english: "And a Torah scroll in his arm and reads" - And the same law applies that it is forbidden to recite by heart.
